limitations: These are headless code, filesystem and mocked-transport tests; they do not prove live VS Code UI behavior or successful delivery to a production model.
Positive loaded receipts can suppress a repeat send. Missing or partially loaded history is not proof that a message was never delivered; uncertain sends must remain paused.
The read transport has no cancellation API. A truly hung read is retained instead of multiplying RPCs, and recovery may require reconnection or reload.
An unverified or live lock owner is intentionally not deleted. Legacy writer.lock files require inspection after old extension hosts close.
The separate journal is not reverse-synchronized to native extension storage. Rollback must retain and expose saved messages for review.
Injected source changes are pinned to official release hashes; a different upstream build requires a new review and both runtime checks.
manualUserChecks: After installation and restart, send several sequential messages in a new chat; verify that each appears and receives one response.
While an answer is running, send two follow-ups; check delivery in queue mode and then in steer mode.
Use Stop with a pending message; check the saved message, resume action and a newly sent message with identical text.
Delete and Undo a saved message; with two windows open, verify that an older window does not restore deleted text or erase the restored message.
Restart with a saved or uncertain message; check that it remains visible and is not silently executed again.
Check text and image attachments, visible recovery controls and saved-message warnings. These UI checks are performed by the user, not by automation.
